jp: 友[とも]だちのチームは強[つよ]い相手[あいて]に次々[つぎつぎ]勝[か]って、ついに決勝[けっしょう]まで{勝[か]ち上[あ]がりました|cv-ageru}。
en: My friend's team beat strong opponents one after another and finally advanced all the way to the final.
d: 勝[か]ち誇[ほこ]りました
why: 勝ち上がる means to move up through the rounds by winning; 上がる gives the 'advance upward' sense.

jp: 友[とも]だちの家[いえ]で、ご飯[はん]が{炊[た]き上[あ]がる|cv-ageru}のを待[ま]っています。
en: I'm waiting at my friend's house for the rice to finish cooking.
why: 〜上がる marks completion: the rice is done cooking by itself (intransitive), so 炊き上がる.

jp: 友[とも]だちが落[お]とした本[ほん]を、私[わたし]は急[いそ]いで{拾[ひろ]い上[あ]げて|cv-ageru}渡[わた]しました。
en: I quickly picked up the book my friend had dropped and handed it over.
why: 拾い上げる is to pick something up off the floor; 上げる supplies the upward movement.

jp: 友[とも]だちと見[み]た映画[えいが]のラストで、うれしさと悲[かな]しさが胸[むね]に{込[こ]み上[あ]げて|cv-ageru}きた。
en: At the end of the movie we saw together, joy and sadness welled up in my chest.
why: Feelings that rise up from within are 込み上げる; none of the other verbs can take a feeling as subject like this.

jp: 三人[さんにん]で、夏[なつ]の旅行[りょこう]の計画[けいかく]を一週間[いっしゅうかん]かけて{練[ね]り上[あ]げました|cv-ageru}。
en: The three of us worked on our summer trip plan for a week until it was polished.
d: 練[ね]り歩[ある]きました
練[ね]り合[あ]わせました
練[ね]り固[かた]めました
why: 練り上げる means to work something out thoroughly until it is finished, which fits a plan refined over a week.

jp: 友[とも]だちはゴールが決[き]まると、「やった！」と叫[さけ]んで拳[こぶし]を空[そら]に{突[つ]き上[あ]げた|cv-ageru}。
en: When the goal went in, my friend shouted 'Yes!' and thrust a fist up into the air.
why: 突き上げる is to thrust upward, the natural verb for a victory fist raised to the sky.
